claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast, BCC-based refractory high-entropy alloy with few second-phase precipitates or a coarse, non-hierarchical microstructure.
Forging followed by annealing at 1100–1200 °C will produce nanoscale, uniformly distributed B2 precipitates in a BCC RHEA matrix.
Forging followed by annealing at 1100–1200 °C will produce a fine, stable dispersion of Laves precipitates in a BCC RHEA matrix.
A continuous BCC matrix containing discrete B2 precipitates can provide a favorable combination of strength and ductility.
Nanoscale B2 or Laves precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby strengthen the alloy.
Laves precipitates can improve ductility in the proposed BCC RHEA architecture.
B2 or Laves precipitates act as sinks for irradiation defects such as voids and helium bubbles.
Defect absorption by the precipitates will limit irradiation-defect accumulation and preserve mechanical strength and ductility.
The intervention will increase yield strength by approximately 20% or more relative to a comparable RHEA lacking designed stable precipitates.
The intervention will improve retention of ductility under combined high-temperature and irradiation exposure.
The precipitate-containing hierarchical microstructure will maintain thermal stability at reactor-relevant temperatures.
The precipitate-containing hierarchical microstructure will maintain stability under heavy-ion or neutron irradiation.
The proposed mechanical benefits should hold at temperatures of at least 1000 °C.
Annealing above approximately 1300 °C may coarsen or destabilize the nanoscale precipitates.
Brittle intermetallic precipitates, including some Laves or Cr/V-rich phases, may reduce ductility or cause embrittlement.
Extended exposure at higher neutron flux may cause unforeseen phase transformations.
Evidence concerning very-high-dose neutron irradiation and extremely long exposure at elevated temperature is limited.
Failure to improve post-irradiation high-temperature mechanical performance, or extensive precipitate coarsening or dissolution, would falsify the hypothesis.
